item.title: How to Lower Your Electric Bill: The Complete Guide (2026)
item.description:
Quick Answer

You can cut your electric bill 20–40% with the highest-ROI moves: raise summer AC to 78°F (or drop winter heat to 68°F) saving $100–$300/year, switch to LEDs ($75/year), lower the water heater to 120°F ($40–$80/year), seal air leaks ($60–$200/year), shift laundry and dishwashing to off-peak hours, and kill vampire loads with smart strips ($50–$180/year).

  • Heating and cooling drive 40–50% of home energy costs — start there.
  • Most utilities run a free home energy audit; call before you spend a dollar.

item.title: Best Smart Plugs to Eliminate Standby Power Drain
item.description:
Disclosure: Some links in this article are affiliate links. If you buy through them, we may earn a small commission at no extra cost to you. This never affects our recommendations — see our affiliate disclosure.

Quick Answer

Smart plugs cut phantom loads — but only if you measure first. Standby power costs the average US household roughly $100–$200 a year (5–10% of residential electricity use). The must-have feature is energy monitoring: find the multi-watt offenders clustered at entertainment centers and home offices, then let schedules cut them automatically. Realistic savings run $50–$150 a year; a $30 four-pack aimed at the right targets breaks even around month six.
